doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Tap dancing and the tramp-band mugger
summary: He learns tap dancing from his father and describes how dancers and a mugger fronted the tramp bands.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, all during this time, I was tap dancing. I learned to tap dance about 1931, maybe before that -- my real father used to dance and he showed me the

timestep. And there was somebody -- in any neighborhood that you lived in, somebody -- everybody could sing or dance or do the time step; what they used to call the "B.S. Chorus"-- "Shim Sham Shimmee", and all the Bucking Wings, and Knee Falls, Splits, (unintelligible); it seemed like it was second nature to me.
As I said, just about everybody could dance.
What kind of a setup did you have in the band where you were playing the fiddle, did you tap dance with the tramp bands?

Well, you know, whoever could dance could with the tramp band. We'd play a tune, and maybe the next tune somebody would get out and dance. But we had what you would call a leader. He wasn't a leader who directed the band, but he was what we called a 'mugger' -- he'd get out in front and go through all kinds of wild antics, and like I say, being in a tramp band, we'd wear any kind of clothes, you know, just to look funny. And that was the times, you might say, they were the only clothes you could get.
Well, that was -- I was growing up, you might say, wearing those little tramp outfits with those singing groups.
